etymologies.etymologyHTML: From minimum +‎ -al.

definitions.definition: (mathematics, technical) Among elements of some collection, such that no other element is greater (with respect to some given partial order).
The smallest possible amount, quantity, or degree.
(art) Characterised by the use of simple form or structures.
(music) Characterised by the repetition and gradual alteration of short phrases.
Something very small; a tiny part or fragment.

quote.citation: 1994, David Holbrook, Creativity and Popular Culture, page 37:
quote.text: […]  we seek in explaining mental phenomena and behavior always the "minimals," the little fragments of association, on which the mind is (passively) supposed to be based.

quote.citation: 1987, J. Golden Taylor, Western Literature Association (U.S.), A Literary History of the American West (page 451)
quote.text: […]  identifications with birds, fish, trees, and flowers (and occasionally as relief, with the stillness of rocks, clam shells, driftwood, and nature's minimals);  […]
